meta.fieldRules: Each figure: value, unit, currency, url, publisher, date, sourceType, confirmed. confirmed=true only when the figure was read on the cited page (directly or from the page's own PDF/JSON-LD). sourceType values: primary (agency/regulator/maker/retailer own page), secondary (press or aggregator), derived (arithmetic on cited figures, shown in note). Null where not published or not found.

tseloniSecurityProtectionFactors.definition: SPF = odds of burglary with no security / odds with the device(s). SPF 12 means one-twelfth the risk. CSEW 2008/09-2011/12. Tseloni, Thompson, Grove, Tilley, Farrell, 'The effectiveness of burglary security devices', Security Journal 30(2):646-664 (2017).

uncertain: FBI 2019 average loss per burglary ($2,661) could not be read on ucr.fbi.gov (Cloudflare). A search summary also claimed a residential-dwelling average of $8,290, which does not fit FBI Table 23 patterns and was left out.

No single-year residential-only burglary figure was found for NYC, Los Angeles, Toronto or London. The counts given include commercial burglary, so derived per-household rates overstate residential risk. California's 38.9% residential share is the only confirmed split.
NY State 137 per 100k (2024) comes from USAFacts, not DCJS. DCJS 2024 final data was not located.
Vancouver 546 residential break-ins (2025) may cover only the Downtown Eastside task-force area, not the whole city.
Mexico City has no confirmed full-year 2025 robo a casa habitación count. Reported cases badly undercount real incidence (INEGI ENVIPE cifra negra of about 90%+).

Ireland's 8,469 Burglary & Related offences for 2025 is national and not residential-only. The CSO page text compared it with 9,461 and a 2022 label, which looks like a page-summary glitch; the -10% figure is from the CSO sentence.
The CSEW rates (13.5 per 1,000 households) are for England and Wales, not London. London's rate is higher, but no confirmed London survey rate was found.

Retailer AC prices from Home Depot US, Canadian Tire, Currys and Argos came from search-result snippets because those sites block automated fetching. Only Home Depot México (8,199 MXN) was read on the page.
The window AC wattage is derived from EER arithmetic, not from a published spec sheet.
BC Hydro: the tiered page shows 11.87 / 14.08 c/kWh and 23.44 c/day, while a search summary gave 11.72 for fiscal 2026. The page value is used.
The CFE Tarifa 1 prices come from a republisher because CFE's own page failed TLS. Block limits vary by season and are not confirmed.
The ChargePoint Home Flex price and installation ranges are unconfirmed; the store did not render prices.
Sonos prices are unconfirmed (sonos.com returns 403). The Mexico figure is the 2021 launch price.

PS5: a secondary site (tech-insider.org) claims Sony reversed the US April 2026 increase on 21 Aug 2026 ($549.99). This was not verified on the PlayStation Blog and may be confused with the 20 Aug 2025 US change, so the UK and Ireland RRPs may be out of date. Canada ($819.99 at Best Buy) and Mexico are unconfirmed.
Samsung UK's page carries both £799 (offer in JSON-LD) and £849. Canada and Mexico prices are promotions; the list prices are given in the units.
UK insurer alarm discounts: no insurer's own page with a fixed percentage was found. The 2-15% (Which?) and 5-20% (ABI) figures are second-hand.

The Tseloni SPFs come from CSEW 2008/09-2011/12 and are observational (a quasi-natural experiment), not causal estimates. The finding that an alarm alone has an SPF below 1 may reflect repeat victims fitting alarms after being burgled.
